workload.resourceFormatCoverage: All formats are measured at catalog sizes 100 and 1000; size 1 uses JSON.
workload.prompts: Required size argument rendered to one text message.
workload.exporterWait: No exporter is configured. Activity and metric listeners consume synchronously; logging uses an in-memory provider.

methodology.startup: Builder composition, service provider creation, hosted validators, and Kestrel start.
methodology.httpNegotiation: Official MCP SDK client creation and protocol initialize after server startup.
methodology.stdioStartupNegotiation: SDK stdio transport combines child-process launch and initialize; reported as one measurement.
methodology.discovery: Tool/resource-template/prompt listing measured independently before warmed primitive operations.
methodology.latency: Sequential wall-clock operation samples; p50, p95, mean and every raw sample are retained.
methodology.allocations: Process-wide managed bytes during the separate throughput batch divided by operations; HTTP includes client and in-process server; stdio measures the parent client process.
methodology.adapterDelta: MCP measurements and direct/REST controls are separate rows; derived paired differences include client and transport cost.
methodology.adapterOnly: The adapter-only rows call the registered Portia tool InvokeAsync method or the registered resource-read/prompt-get handler from the host's MCP server options. The MCP server dispatch pipeline, JSON-RPC serialization, client and transport are excluded. RequestContext and configured per-request service scope are created for every call before the latency timer starts. P50/P95/mean cover only the direct Portia adapter handler invocation; result validation runs after the latency timer. Throughput and process allocations cover the repeated direct-call loop including request-context and scope setup, but not result validation, protocol dispatch, client or transport.
